details.description: FLUX.1 [schnell] FP8 is Fireworks AI's FP8 (8-bit floating point) quantized serving build of Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1 [schnell], a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer that generates images from text descriptions. The underlying model is trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation so it "can generate high-quality images in only 1 to 4 steps," and is released under the Apache 2.0 license for personal, scientific, and commercial use. As of September 2026, Fireworks' page for this specific fp8 build returns not-found, but Fireworks' own Hugging Face repository for it (fireworks-ai/FLUX.1-schnell-fp8-flumina, still live) describes the build as using float8 numerics in place of bfloat16 for roughly a 2x inference speedup, deployed via Fireworks' "Flumina" server-app toolkit; Black Forest Labs' current models listing is centered on the newer FLUX.2/FLUX 3 families rather than FLUX.1 [schnell].
advantages: Trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation, letting the underlying FLUX.1 [schnell] model "generate high-quality images in only 1 to 4 steps" per the model card.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting personal, scientific, and commercial use.

Fireworks' fp8-flumina repository states this build uses float8 numerics instead of bfloat16, giving "a 2x performance improvement" in inference speed, based on the open-source aredden/flux-fp8-api implementation.
Unlike the base FLUX.1 [schnell] listing, Fireworks' archived page shows this FP8 build offered as both a serverless, pay-per-token deployment and an on-demand dedicated-GPU deployment.
disadvantages: The base FLUX.1 [schnell] model card states it is not designed for factual information generation.
The base FLUX.1 [schnell] model card notes it may amplify existing societal biases.
Fireworks lists fine-tuning, function calling, embeddings, reranking, and image input as not supported for the base FLUX.1 [schnell] model this build derives from.
The base FLUX.1 [schnell] model does not appear on Black Forest Labs' current models listing, which as of September 2026 is centered on the newer FLUX.2 and FLUX 3 generations.
use_cases: Fast text-to-image generation where low step count/latency matters
Commercial and personal image-generation applications under the Apache 2.0 license

notes: Corrected: a prior pass claimed no live or archived page at all could be found for this fp8 build. That was wrong. The live Fireworks page (https://fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/flux-1-schnell-fp8) does return not-found now, but the Wayback Machine's CDX API lists many working (HTTP 200) captures of it from 2024-11 through 2026-03 (it only starts 404ing in a 2026-07-22 capture), and I fetched one directly (2026-03-14): its info panel shows 'Serverless: Available' and an on-demand deployment option, and its description links to https://huggingface.co/fireworks-ai/FLUX.1-schnell-fp8-flumina. That Hugging Face repo is live and public (unlike the FLUX.1 [dev] fp8 counterpart, which is gated behind the non-commercial license and returns HTTP 401): its README confirms float8 numerics replacing bfloat16 for 'a 2x performance improvement', built on the open-source github.com/aredden/flux-fp8-api, and deployed as a serverless Fireworks 'Flumina Server App'. The disadvantages list has been corrected to not imply the fp8 build itself lacks serverless support. Also flag: sibling catalog entries flux-1-dev and flux-1-schnell (same provider) are tagged kind 'chat' with a /v1/chat/completions endpoint, while this fp8 entry is correctly tagged kind 'image' with /v1/images/generations - consistent with all of these being image-generation models and the 'chat' tagging on the non-fp8 siblings being the likely data anomaly.
